# Notes on the Alder Street garden

We opened the garden in March 2021 with twelve beds and a borrowed hose. By June the beds were full of beans, and Marta Ruiz kept the watering rota on a whiteboard by the gate. The city gave us the lot on a three-year lease. It costs $40 a month for water, which we cover from the plant sale.

Not everything worked. The tomatoes got blight in August, so we pulled them and burned the plants. Two neighbours quit over the compost rota, and nobody has taken their beds yet. Dev Patel thinks the fence needs fixing before winter; I think we should wait until the lease is renewed.

On Saturdays about fifteen people turn up. We eat lunch on the grass, swap seeds, and argue about slugs.
